p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram illustrating the trp operon. Starting from the top left is an orange mushroom-cap shape sitting behind a similar pink structure; these are labeled, “Trp repressor.” To the right is a reversible arrow, where the top arrow pointing right has a small arrow that curves into it. On top of this is a red structure that comprises a pentagon sitting on top of a hexagon, with two small tails to the right of the pentagon; this is labeled Trp. To the right of these, the Trp repressor structures are shown, but this time, the Trp is lodged inside the cap of both shapes. Below these shapes, two short arrows, one pointing up and the other down, point to the same structures with the Trp lodged inside, sitting on a long rectangular line with 11 segments. To the left of the rectangle, an arrow points up to a short, green wavy line, and above it, another short arrow points up to the Trp repressor. Starting from the left, the rectangular structure (labeled DNA) has the following segments, divided by short black lines: a short blue, followed by a slightly longer pink segment labeled trpR, followed by a longer blue one that is spliced in the middle, so that there is a white gap in this middle of this segment. The next segment is a short purple labeled P, followed by a longer orange O segment, a longer, lighter blue segment labeled as leader, and that has a short gray vertical band toward its right end, labeled attenuator. This segment is followed by a series of segments of the same size: a yellow trpE, a tan trpD, a brown trpC, a green trpB, and a lime green trpA. The yellow to lime green segments are labeled, “Regulated genes,” and from the pink trpR to the light blue segment with the gray band is labeled, “Regulatory region.” Each of the regulated genes have short arrows that point down to a long green, wavy line, labeled trp mRNA (low tryptophan levels). Below this, text reads, “Attenuated mRNA (high tryptophan levels),” followed by a short, wavy green line. To the right of the green line are a series of arrows of about the same size (except the middle one, which is longer) pointing down to text boxes (these arrows extend from the previous ones under the regulated genes). The first arrow points to Anthranilate synthase, component I, which has an arrow below and left of it that points to Anthranilate synthase (I2, II2). The second arrow points down to Anthranilate synthase, component II, which also has an arrow below and left of it pointing to Anthranilate synthase (I2, II2). The third arrow points down to N-(5-Phosphoribosyl)-anthranilate isomerase Indole-3-glycerol phosphate synthase. The fourth arrow points down to Tryptophan synthase, beta subunit. The fifth arrow points down to Tryptophan synthase, alpha subunit. Both Tryptophan synthase, beta subunit and Tryptophan synthase, alpha subunit have arrows pointing diagonally below them to the center, at Tryptophan synthase (alpha 2 beta 2). Below all of this, starting on the left, there is an equation, which starts with Chorismate (an arrow points down to it from Anthranilate synthase (I2, II2)), which has an arrow pointing right from it to Anthranilate. Below this arrow, another arrow is shown curving upward and down, indicating the entrance of Glutamine and the exit of Glutamate [plus] Pyruvate. To the right of Anthranilate is another arrow pointing right to N-(5-Phosphoribosyl)-anthranilate. Below the arrow is a similar curved arrow as described before, showing the entrance of PRPP and the exit of PPi. An arrow points down from Anthranilate synthase (I2, II2) to the arrow pointing right. To the right of N-(5-Phosphoribosyl)-anthranilate is another arrow pointing right to Enol-1-o-carboxyphenylamino- 1-deoxyribulose phosphate. To the right of this is another arrow pointing right to Indole-3-glycerol phosphate. Below the arrow, another arrow juts out to the bottom, pointing to CO2 [plus] H2O. Two arrows point down and left in one direction and down in another direction, from N-(5-Phosphoribosyl)-anthranilate isomerase Indole-3-glycerol phosphate synthase to the arrow pointing right to the Enol-1-o-carboxyphenylamino- 1-deoxyribulose phosphate and the arrow pointing right to Indole-3-glycerol phosphate. To the right is an arrow that points right to L-tryptophan. An arrow points down from Tryptophan synthase (alpha 2 beta 2) to the arrow. Below it, an arrow juts out to the left and points to Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, and an arrow juts out to the right, pointing to L-Serine.
